questions.stem: The 30-year-old male has total body water is 60% of the body weight. What are the proportions of ECF and ICF?
questions.solutionHtml:
20,40

When expressed as the percentage of body weight, 40% of body weight is in ICF (2/3rd of 60%), and 20% of body weight is in ECF (1/3rd of 60%).




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 4.

questions.stem: Why is Homeostasis defined as a state of balance between continuing processes?

options.label: A
options.text: All variables are given equal importance

options.label: B
options.text: Body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits

options.label: C
options.text: Can achieve a constancy in extreme environmental challenges

options.label: D
options.text: The set point for all homeostatic variables is always fixed

questions.answerText: Body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits
questions.solutionHtml:
Body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits

Homeostasis is called dynamic equilibrium because the body maintains an internal balance within fluctuating limits.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no: 4

questions.stem: An Industrial laborer moves in March from Kashmir to Delhi and becomes acclimatized by working outdoors for a month. Compared with his responses on the first few days in Delhi, for the same activity level after acclimatization, one would expect higher:
questions.solutionHtml:
Sweating rate
  • Among the most important physiological changes that occur during this acclimatization process are an approximately two-fold increase in the maximum rate of sweating, an increase in plasma volume, and diminished loss of salt in the sweat and urine to almost none; the last two effects result from increased secretion of aldosterone by the adrenal glands.

questions.stem: A primigravida with 38 completed weeks of gestation has gone into labor. Oxytocin was started to augment labor. The secondary messenger system through which oxytocin acts is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Phospholipase c

The second messenger system through which oxytocin acts is the Phospholipase C system

questions.stem: A 61-year-old male with erectile dysfunction asks his physician to prescribe Viagra (sildenafil). Viagra produces its physiological effects by blocking the enzyme that hydrolyses the secondary messenger by which nitric oxide produces its physiological effects. Which of the following is the secondary messenger?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyclic GMP
  • Sildenafil (sold under the brand name Viagra) inhibits PDE-5, increasing cyclic guanosine monophosphate cGMP to allow smooth-muscle relaxation by prolonging the action of NO.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 31-35

questions.stem: A 43-year-old pregnant woman develops preeclampsia at 32 weeks gestation. Magnesium sulfate, which interacts with NMDA receptors in the central nervous system, is ordered for the prevention of eclamptic seizures until the fetus can be delivered. Which of the following activates the NMDA receptor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glutamate

MgSO4 also acts centrally to inhibit NMDA receptors, providing anticonvulsant activity by increasing the seizure threshold.

  • The NMDA receptor channel is a large channel permeable to Ca2+, K+, and Na+
  • It is activated by glutamate, but unlike other glutamate receptor channels, the NMDA channel is blocked by Mg2+ in its resting state.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 98, 108–110

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman consults a dermatologist to evaluate and treat her glabellar lines (frown lines on the forehead just above the nose). After her treatment options are explained, the patient asks the dermatologist to administer Botox (botulinum type A). Botox injections smooth out glabellar lines by which of the following methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Blocking the release of synaptic transmitters from α-motoneurons

options.label: B
options.text: Preventing the opening of sodium channels on muscle membranes

options.label: C
options.text: Decreasing the amount of calcium released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

options.label: D
options.text: Increasing the flow of blood into the facial muscle

questions.answerText: Blocking the release of synaptic transmitters from α-motoneurons
questions.solutionHtml:
Blocking the release of synaptic transmitters from α-motoneurons

Botulinum toxin inhibits the release of acetylcholine from α-motoneurons by blocking proteins responsible for the fusion of the synaptic channel with the presynaptic membrane.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 87–88.

questions.stem: A 76-year-old woman with a history of uncontrolled hypertension presents in the Emergency Department with hypotension and shock-like symptoms. Her daughter reported systolic blood pressure near 200 mmHg earlier in the day. The clinician suspects a dissecting aneurysm, which is confirmed with a CT of the chest. A biopsy of the repaired aorta shows giant cell arteritis, and the woman is placed on a regimen of high-dose prednisone. The anti-inflammatory effect of exogenous glucocorticoids is thought to be due to which of the following?

options.label: C
options.text: Increased release of interleukin-1 (pyrogen) from granulocytes

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of the activation of NF-Kb

questions.answerText: Inhibition of the activation of NF-Kb
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of the activation of NF-Kb

Glucocorticoids inhibit the activation of NF-kB by increasing the production of IkBa, and this is probably the main basis of their anti-inflammatory action.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 371–372, 636

questions.stem: Although more than 400 blood groups have been identified, the ABO blood group system remains the most important in clinical medicine because:

options.label: A
options.text: It was the first blood group system to be discovered

options.label: B
options.text: It has four different blood groups A, B, AB, O(H)

options.label: C
options.text: ABO (H) antigens are present in most body tissues and fluids

options.label: D
options.text: ABO (H) antibodies are invariably present in plasma when a person’s RBC lacks the corresponding antigen

questions.answerText: ABO (H) antibodies are invariably present in plasma when a person’s RBC lacks the corresponding antigen
questions.solutionHtml:
ABO (H) antibodies are invariably present in plasma when a person’s RBC lacks the corresponding antigen

This is not present with other blood group antigens. For example, an Rh-negative individual does not have Anti-Rh antibodies unless the person came in contact with Rh-positive blood.

Therefore, ABO typing is clinically responsible for the maximum number of transfusion reactions.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 527

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is true about the process shown in the given Image below?

options.label: A
options.text: A carrier protein is required in this process

options.label: B
options.text: It occurs along the concentration gradient

options.label: C
options.text: It occurs against the concentration gradient

options.label: D
options.text: Secretory products like hormones pass through this process

questions.answerText: Secretory products like hormones pass through this process
questions.solutionHtml:
Secretory products like hormones pass through this process

The process shown in the image is exocytosis and it is an energy-independent process. Exocytosis is required for the transport of hormones.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 47

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man visits his family doctor, complaining about a fever. The blood test revealed elevated neutrophils. The elevated Neutrophils will reach the infection site by crossing the walls of blood vessels.The flexibility of cells is due to this compositions of cell membrane:
questions.solutionHtml:
All the above

The flexibility of the cell membrane is a function of lipids. This is due to the presence of unsaturated fatty acids e.g., Oleic acid and linoleic acid

questions.stem: Lipids constitute 40-45% of the cell membrane, mainly the phospholipid. They are arranged in a bilayer to avoid rupture of the membrane, since one end of the phospholipid is polar whereas the other is non-polar. Which statement is true about the polarity of the membrane is:

options.label: A
options.text: Head consists of phosphate anion and is hydrophobic

options.label: B
options.text: Tail consists of non-polar hydrophilic end

options.label: C
options.text: Head is non-polar, whereas tail is polar

questions.solutionHtml:
Head is polar and hydrophilic

The head is polar and it's hydrophilic, therefore option D is the only correct answer.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 15

questions.stem: A 38-year-old male visits the hospital, with difficulty in breathing and coughing. He says, it occurs mainly at night and feels chest pain also. The doctor noticed a wheezing sound also and after examining the patient carefully and concluded that it was Asthma and prescribed him steroids. Which statement is true about the entry of steroids into the cell?

options.label: A
options.text: Lipid of cell membrane helps steroids to enter

options.label: B
options.text: Protein carrier helps steroids to enter the cell

options.label: C
options.text: Steroids do not enter the cell but act through cell surface receptors

options.label: D
options.text: Steroids are water-soluble and act through aquaporins

questions.answerText: Lipid of cell membrane helps steroids to enter
questions.solutionHtml:
Lipid of cell membrane helps steroids to enter

Steroids are lipid-soluble hormones and therefore their entry through the cell membrane is quite smooth because a big constituent of the cell membrane is lipid. So they diffuse into the cell membrane being soluble in lipids. Therefore, option A is true. Rest are false.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 16

questions.stem: You are giving a presentation on the cell membrane structure in your class. While presenting your professor asked that the plasma membrane is made up of a lipid bilayer which determines the ability of substances to move in and out of the cell. Which of the following substances are lipid soluble and water soluble respectively?

options.label: A
options.text: Lipid soluble- CO2 and O2 ,water-soluble-sodium and glucose

options.label: B
options.text: Lipid soluble- O2 and glucose, water-soluble- Na+ and k+

options.label: C
options.text: Lipid soluble- CO2 and glucose, water-soluble- Na+ and O2

options.label: D
options.text: Lipid soluble- CO2 and O2, water-soluble- steroid hormones and k+

questions.answerText: Lipid soluble- CO2 and O2 ,water-soluble-sodium and glucose
questions.solutionHtml:
Lipid soluble- CO2 and O2 ,water-soluble-sodium and glucose

Small lipid-soluble substances can easily pass through the plasma membrane without any transporters and channels. These substances include O2, CO2, fatty acids, and some steroid hormones.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 54

questions.stem: You are a medical student and you are allotted a topic to present in class. The topic given to you was excitation-contraction coupling. It is a process in which muscle cells are stimulated to contract and it is followed by muscle cell relaxation. It involves the following events.Action potential Calcium release into the cytoplasmCross-bridge cyclingCytoplasmic calcium removalDepolarization of T tubulesWhich of the following options lists the correct sequence of events for excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscle tissue?Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,5,2,3,4

Action potential comes and causes Depolarization of T tubules which causes calcium release into the cytoplasm. Free calcium binds to troponin C on actin filaments and causes a conformational change and exposes a site on the actin molecule that binds to the myosin head which results in ATP hydrolysis and produces crossbridge cycling. And producing a contraction. Finally calcium is re-sequestrated back into ER to allow relaxation to occur.

'

So the correct sequence is A.





Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 55

questions.stem: Which of the following is the approximate extracellular fluid volume of a normal individual?
questions.solutionHtml:
20% of body mass
  • Sixty percent of the body mass is water.
  • Of this water, one-third (20% of body mass) is extracellular and two-thirds (40% of body mass) is intracellular.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1–3, 6–7

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding auto-regulation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Maintains the blood flow

The capacity of tissues to regulate their blood flow is referred to as autoregulation.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 563
